Subject: Post-demo: inference cost & feature-level payback (HealthMate)

Hi Emily — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we don’t lose momentum.

Call summary (30m):
- Primary use case: triage assistant and outpatient follow-up summaries for clinicians (avg. 420 tokens per interaction).
- Target SLA: p95 latency < 350ms on text-gen for patient-facing experiences.
- Expected ramp: pilot 5k daily active interactions -> scale to 50k over 9 months.
- Budget guardrail: initial procurement has ~$120k ARR budget for inference and monitoring.

Immediate asks:
1) We promised a unit-econ sketch. See attached "redwood_unit_econ_model.xlsx" — a conservative baseline and an upside scenario.
2) Please confirm expected average tokens per session and expected daily interactions for the pilot (Emily/Carlos).
3) If procurement wants standard T&Cs, share contact and we’ll run a redline with legal.

Key numbers from the attached (conservative):
- Baseline token volume: 5k sessions/day * 420 tokens = 2.1M tokens/day (~63M tokens/month).
- Target price sensitivity: $/1M tokens needs to hit ~$18–$26 to meet your desired margin band once application-level revenue is accounted for.
- Feature-level view: triage feature target $/feature/month = $0.75–$1.20 (depends on reuse and caching).

Next steps: I’ll follow up with a detailed unit-econ email and two pricing options (pilot and committed). Marissa, Ben — please review the attached model and note any quick changes before I send the pricing note to HealthMate.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Emily — great context. Below is a concise pilot vs committed offer, plus a short CAC/payback snapshot. I’m attaching a simplified model and the assumptions tab for transparency.

Pilot (3 months, month-to-month):
- Price: $34 / 1M tokens (pilot) — includes 24/7 pilot support (standard) and basic telemetry retention.
- Volume: conservative baseline 3k DAU * 420 tokens = ~38M tokens / month.
- Monthly cost (inference-only) at our pilot price: 38 * $34 = $1,292 / month? (NOTE: this math is illustrative; see attached for full calc)

Committed (12-month, 1-year commit):
- Tiered discounts: 1) 0–30M tokens/mo: $28 / 1M; 2) 30–80M tokens/mo: $20 / 1M; 3) >80M tokens/mo: $15 / 1M.
- For your expected ramp to 63M tokens/mo, blended price ~ $22/1M tokens.

Feature-level economics (triage assistant):
- Per-interaction inference cost (best-guess, committed pricing): 420 tokens * $0.000022 = $0.00924 per interaction.
- If you monetize per completed triage at $0.75, gross margin contribution per interaction ~ 88% before CAC and infra.

CAC & payback (back-of-envelope):
- Assume sales & onboarding CAC for similar accounts: $60k for pilot conversion + 6 months of CSM (variable).
- At 3k DAU, monetized interactions 60% -> monthly revenue ~ 3k * 0.6 * 30 days * $0.75 = $40,500/month.
- Payback on $60k CAC at that run-rate: ~1.5 months (fast) — this is illustrative; if conversion is lower or prices per feature are reduced the payback extends. CFO target <9 months looks fully achievable under committed pricing assumptions.

A couple of clarifications I’ll fold into the formal quote:
- Confirm whether patient flows will be monetized or internal (we treated them as internal in the model).
- Retention/caching assumptions: we applied a 14% effective token reduction from prefix/KV caching for repeated clinician prompts. If your flows are less repetitive the effective cost will be higher.

I’ll loop Marissa on the formal quote and Ben on CAC assumptions. Attaching: redwood_unit_econ_model.xlsx (filtered 'HealthMate' scenario).

Thanks,
Aditya

Attachment: redwood_unit_econ_model.xlsx (filtered 'HealthMate' scenario)

Emily / team — quick note on CAC and packaging from a growth lens.

Two packaging recommendations that improve payback without lowering per-token economics too much:
1) Usage + seat hybrid for clinician admin features — charge small per-seat fee ($6–$8/admin/mo) for configuration/support; this converts some fixed costs into recurring revenue and shortens CAC payback.
2) Minimum committed window for pilots (6 weeks) with a small onboarding fee ($5k) to cover initial SRE/CSM effort. That fee is capitalized into ARR and materially shortens payback.

Effect on payback: with a $5k onboarding fee + $6/admin/mo on 30 admins, incremental revenue month 1 = $5k + (30*$6) = $5,180 -> reduces payback materially.

Happy to sketch a one-pager that maps the combos to payback months for CFO review. Marissa — can you confirm typical onboarding SRE days we should assume for HealthMate?

Best,
Ben Carter
VP Growth | Redwood Inference
